title: Graph Structural Attack by Perturbing Spectral Distance

problem.claim: Graph Convolutional Networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks.

gap.claim: The paper addresses disruption of the graph spectral filters that theoretically underpin GCNs.

contributions.claim: Defines spectral distance from graph Laplacian eigenvalues to measure disruption of spectral filters.
Realizes a graph structural attack by maximizing spectral distance and introduces an efficient approximation to reduce eigen-decomposition time complexity.
Reports attack effectiveness across black-box and white-box test-time evasion and training-time poisoning settings.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments demonstrate the reported attack's effectiveness in black-box and white-box settings for both test-time evasion and training-time poisoning attacks.
Qualitative analysis suggests a connection between imposed Fourier-domain spectral changes and attack behavior in the spatial domain.

narrative_sequence.summary: GCNs perform well on graph learning tasks but are vulnerable to adversarial attacks.
The attack targets graph spectral filters in the Fourier domain.
Spectral distance based on graph Laplacian eigenvalues measures filter disruption.
The attack maximizes spectral distance and uses an approximation to reduce eigen-decomposition cost.
Experiments and qualitative analysis report effectiveness and relate spectral changes to spatial-domain attack behavior.
